rationale: Direct phenotypic descriptions of individuals with bi-allelic SGSM3 pathogenic variants (MRT84) show speech delay rather than complete absence of expressive speech. In the index kindred reported by Birnbaum et al., affected individuals presented with delayed speech onset but attained verbal communicative ability, including one patient who achieved age-appropriate language function (developmental quotient of 84). Subsequent reports (such as Turkyilmaz et al.) confirm an intellectual disability phenotype with preserved baseline communicative developmental capacity rather than profound non-verbal encephalopathy.

evidence.text: Affected individuals carrying a homozygous founder variant in SGSM3 manifested delayed speech acquisition rather than complete absence of speech, with one affected child exhibiting normal motor milestones and achieving age-appropriate language skills with a developmental quotient of 84 after delayed speech onset at 5 years.

evidence.text: Two siblings with bi-allelic loss-of-function variants in SGSM3 (c.1576C>T, p.Arg526Ter) presented with nonsyndromic intellectual disability and short stature, confirming consistent presentation as intellectual disability with developmental delay rather than severe non-verbal neurodegenerative phenotypes.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: In this study, a novel homozygous stop-gain (NM_015705.6: c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) variation was detected in the SGSM3 gene in two siblings with short stature and ID findings.

evidence.text: Clinical synopsis and nosology of autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-84 (MRT84) classify the condition as developmental delay, short stature, and dysmorphic features rather than anarthria or complete absence of speech.

new_directions.question_text: What is the long-term expressive vocabulary and syntax complexity trajectory in adults with bi-allelic SGSM3 truncating versus missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: While early childhood speech delay is documented, formal standardized speech-language assessments in mature post-pubertal cohorts will clarify if speech apraxia resolves completely or leaves residual expressive deficits.
